question: Which feature in Windows allows you to recover files that were accidentally deleted?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Recycle Bin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Recycle Bin** is a feature in Microsoft Windows that temporarily stores files and folders deleted by the user.
 
• It allows users to recover accidentally deleted files until the bin is emptied, ensuring data safety in case of errors.
 
• Files in the Recycle Bin can be restored to their original location using the "Restore" option.
 
• The Recycle Bin does not store files deleted from external drives or removed via Shift+Delete, as these actions bypass the bin.
 
• This feature has been included in Windows operating systems since Windows 95 and remains a critical utility for file recovery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **File Recovery in Windows:**

 
 
• Files deleted via Shift+Delete or from external drives can be recovered using third-party tools or backup software.
 
• Windows provides a **File History** feature to back up and restore files periodically, offering an alternative to Recycle Bin recovery.
 
 
 
• **Disk Cleanup:**
 
 
• Disk Cleanup is a Windows utility designed to free up space by removing unnecessary files such as temporary files and cached data.
 
• It does not serve as a file recovery tool.
 
 
 
• **Task Manager:**
 
 
• Task Manager is used for monitoring system performance and managing running applications and processes.
 
• It does not handle file recovery tasks.
 
 
 
• **Control Panel:**
 
 
• The Control Panel in Windows is used for system configuration and settings management.
 
• It does not provide file recovery functionalities.
